fact: Until 1 January 1920 Strijp was an independent municipality; then it merged into Eindhoven together with four neighbouring municipalities.
The merger followed fast industrial and population growth, which caused housing shortages, traffic problems and pressure on local services.
A regional heritage study records the name Strijp in 1418; Strijp became an independent municipality in 1795.
Strijp was once mainly heathland and farmland.
Philips began building Philipsdorp for its workers in 1910, on land that then belonged to Strijp.
On Strijp-S, Philips built a glass factory in 1916, followed by laboratories and other factories.

On 6 December 1942 the Royal Air Force bombed Philips factories in Strijp and central Eindhoven because they made radio parts for German forces; in Strijp the glass factory and the bakelite factory were hit.
After Philips left its old industrial sites, Strijp-S changed from a fenced factory complex into a mixed area with homes, businesses, education, shops, cafes and cultural venues.
Today Strijp is a large Eindhoven city district with Philipsdorp, Strijp-S, Meerhoven, Eindhoven Airport and business parks, and green space such as Philips de Jongh Park and Philips van Lenneppark.
A 2025 housing study, using 2023 CBS figures, counted about 38,300 residents in the current Strijp district.
Coen Dillen, full name Coenraad Henrik Dillen, was born on 5 October 1926 in Strijp.
Coen Dillen was a striker, nicknamed Het Kanon (the cannon) because of his hard shot.
Coen Dillen played for PSV from 1949 to 1961: 328 matches and 287 goals.
In 1956-57, his first Eredivisie season, Coen Dillen scored 43 league goals in 34 matches, a record nobody has matched since.
Coen Dillen played 5 matches for the Netherlands national team between 1954 and 1957 and scored 4 goals.
Professional football started in the Netherlands in 1954; the KNVB gives 25 November 1954 as the start.
Coen Dillen died on 24 July 1990; in 2003 a statue of him was placed at the PSV stadium.
